Corporate & Business Law Practice Guide

Sole Proprietorship vs. Partnership vs. Private Limited Company in Nepal

📅 Published: 2025-05-20
🔄 Updated: 2025-10-01
⏱ 8 min read
🔍 Review: Managing Associate Advocate, High Court Bar Association
Direct Legal Answer & Overview

In Nepal, business structures differ fundamentally in liability, legal personality, and regulation: 1) A Sole Proprietorship (Private Firm) is owned by a single individual with unlimited personal liability and no separate legal identity; 2) A Partnership Firm (governed by the Partnership Act 2020) is formed by two or more partners with joint and unlimited personal liability; and 3) A Private Limited Company (governed by the Companies Act 2063) is an independent corporate entity with limited liability shielding promoters' personal assets, perpetual succession, and the ability to issue equity to outside investors.

Key Practical Takeaways

  • Private Limited Companies provide limited liability; proprietors and partners have unlimited personal liability.
  • Companies can raise equity capital and survive the death of founders.
  • Proprietorships and partnerships have simpler annual compliance requirements.

Choosing the right legal vehicle for your enterprise in Nepal impacts your tax obligations, administrative workload, and—most critically—whether your personal savings and ancestral land are shielded from business debts.

1. Comprehensive Legal Comparison Table

Legal Attribute Sole Proprietorship (निजी फर्म) Partnership Firm (साझेदारी फर्म) Private Limited Company (प्रा.लि.)
Governing Law Private Firm Registration Act 2014 Partnership Act 2020 Companies Act 2063
Regulating Authority Dept of Commerce / Local Municipality Dept of Commerce / Dept of Industry Office of Company Registrar (OCR)
Personal Liability Unlimited: Personal assets can be seized for business debt Joint & Unlimited: Each partner personally liable Limited: Shareholder liability strictly capped at unpaid shares
Separate Entity No independent legal personality No independent corporate personality Yes, independent legal person
Perpetual Succession Dissolves upon death of proprietor Dissolves upon death/exit of partner unless deed provides Perpetual: survives death or bankruptcy of shareholders
Foreign Investment Ineligible for FDI Ineligible for FDI in most sectors Fully eligible for FDI under FITTA 2075

2. Strategic Advice for Entrepreneurs

If you are operating a local retail shop or freelance consultancy with minimal financial debt risk, a Sole Proprietorship offers simple setup. However, if your business hires staff, takes commercial loans, enters high-value contracts, or intends to raise investor equity, incorporating a Private Limited Company is essential to shield your personal wealth behind the corporate veil.

Statutory Citations & Governing Nepal Legislation

Statute / Act Section / Rule Legal Significance
Private Firm Registration Act 2014 Section 3 Rules for registering sole proprietorships with Department of Commerce or Municipalities.
Partnership Act 2020 Section 4 & 5 Partnership formation, joint liability, and Department of Industry registration.
Companies Act 2063 Section 3 & 4 Limited liability corporate personality.

Documentary Checklist for this Procedure

  • ✔ Citizenship Certificates of business owners / partners / promoters
  • ✔ Partnership Deed (for partnerships) or MOA/AOA (for companies)
  • ✔ Rent agreement and municipal location clearance

Frequently Asked Questions on this Topic

Can a Sole Proprietorship in Nepal be converted into a Private Limited Company?

Yes. Under Nepalese commercial procedure, the assets and business goodwill of a registered sole proprietorship can be transferred and integrated into a freshly incorporated Private Limited Company through a formal asset transfer agreement and municipal notification.
